newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SASANI UP ON NEWS WOULDN'T OVERPAY ON BUY.
newsitem.headline: SASANI UP ON NEWS WOULDN'T OVERPAY ON BUY.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Sasani Ltd leapt in early trade on Wednesday after the film equipment and production company said it would not overpay for a stake in entertainment firm Interleisure.

Shortly after the start of the session Sasani rose to 108 cents -- a gain of 12.5 percent in brisk dealings. By 0755 GMT the shares had edged off their peaks to trade at 104 cents, up eight cents in volume of over 1.5 million shares.
"Initially there were rumours that Sasani was planning to pay too much for the Interleisure stake but now that it looks like they are out of the deal, the shares have recovered," one dealer said.
Sasani chairman Nic Frangos told Reuters on Tuesday that it would not overburden itself with debt if the price tag of Interleisure Ltd was too high.
"There is a price at which Sasani will not go beyond in terms of this deal...the worst scenario for Sasani is to buy this company at an unrealistic price," Frangos said.

He questioned whether the firm could be bought at a "realistic" price as several competitive bids were sure to inflate it. Market rumours have said that the price has risen to around 1.5 billion rand from around 1.2 billion before.

Frangos said Sasani would remain a company with strong earnings potential without the Interleisure buy, achieving its forecast 3.6 cents earnings per share for the 15-months to end June from 3.4 cents in the year to March 31.
The sale of Interleisure, which holds a 20 percent stake in Sasani, is part of the unbundling of Servgro International which together with Kersaf Ltd jointly own Interleisure.
Another strong contender for Interleisure is acquisitive media firm Primedia Ltd . Primedia shares were last down 70 cents at 30.00 rand in thin volume of 2,500 shares.
